summary: Built redundant Layer-3 transit between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense), carrying traffic between node3's and node4's private networks with automatic OSPF-based failover across either transit network, then completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes with proven boot-identity changes and recovery.
actions_performed: Discovered topology: node1(VyOS)/node2(OPNsense) joined by two spare NIC pairs (eth1/vtnet1 -> 10.10.1.0/30, eth2/vtnet2 -> 10.10.2.0/30); node1-eth3 to node3-ens7 (10.10.3.0/24 private net); node2-vtnet3 to node4-ens7 (10.10.4.0/24 private net)

Addressed all transit and private-network interfaces: node1 via VyOS set/commit/save, node2 via OPNsense config.xml surgery + rc.configure_interface, node3/node4 via ip addr persisted in /etc/network/interfaces.d
Added static routes on node3/node4 toward each other's private subnet via their local router
Attempted OPNsense gateway-group policy-routing for failover first; found via pf state/tcpdump analysis it doesn't apply symmetrically to bidirectionally-initiated flows, so removed that config

Installed the os-frr plugin on OPNsense (pkg install) and configured OSPF area 0.0.0.0 covering both transit /30 networks and the node4 private /24; rendered config via configctl template reload + quagga restart
Configured native VyOS OSPF (area 0) covering both transit /30 networks and the node3 private /24
Verified Full OSPF adjacencies on both transit links and ECMP kernel routes to the remote private subnet on both routers

Verified baseline node3<->node4 connectivity, then ran a continuous ping while administratively disabling transit-A (node1 eth1); confirmed zero packet loss (186/186 sequential pings, no gaps) as OSPF re-converged onto transit-B within seconds
Re-enabled transit-A and confirmed OSPF re-formed Full adjacency and ECMP routing was restored on both routers
Captured healthy baselines (boot id/boottime, OSPF state, routes, connectivity) on all four nodes
Restarted node3, node4, node1, node2 one at a time via native reboot mechanisms; polled exec until each came back; proved changed boot id (Linux) / kern.boottime (FreeBSD) on every node

Re-verified post-restart: interface addressing, OSPF Full adjacencies, ECMP routes, and end-to-end node3<->node4 ping on every node, including re-persisting node3/node4 network config via ifupdown drop-ins so it survives reboot

evidence.requirement: Redundant path exists between node3 and node4 private networks via two independent transit networks
evidence.summary: Confirmed eth1/vtnet1 (10.10.1.0/30) and eth2/vtnet2 (10.10.2.0/30) as the two independent transit links between node1 and node2, each pingable

evidence.requirement: OSPF dynamic routing established and providing ECMP across both transit networks
evidence.summary: show ip ospf neighbor Full/DR and Full/Backup on both transit links; kernel routes show ECMP nexthops via eth1 and eth2 on node1

evidence.requirement: Traffic continues between node3 and node4 across the failure of one transit network
evidence.summary: Continuous ping from node3 to node4 showed zero gaps across 186 sequential ICMP sequences while transit-A (eth1) was administratively disabled mid-stream and OSPF re-converged onto transit-B in seconds

evidence.requirement: Transit network A restored and full redundancy re-established after the transition
evidence.summary: Re-enabling eth1 restored Full/DR OSPF adjacency and ECMP nexthops via both eth1 and eth2

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured on every node before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id/kern.boottime, OSPF neighbor state, routes, and node3<->node4 ping baselines on all four nodes prior to any restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restarted with proven changed boot identity and recovered service/data state
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from 1f0657c2... to da1cf2a4...; post-restart ens7 IP/route lost (ephemeral), re-applied and persisted via /etc/network/interfaces.d, ping to node4 restored

evidence.requirement: node4 restarted with proven changed boot identity and recovered service/data state
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from 8336c3a1... to 4ee44240...; persisted ens7 config (added before restart) survived reboot; ping to node3 restored automatically

evidence.requirement: node1 (VyOS router) restarted with proven changed boot identity and recovered OSPF/routing state
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from ebd78841... to f5d5fa7b...; VyOS save persisted interface/OSPF config; Full/DR adjacencies and ECMP routes re-established automatically; node3->node4 ping succeeded post-recovery

evidence.requirement: node2 (OPNsense router) restarted with proven changed boot identity and recovered OSPF/routing/interface state
evidence.summary: kern.boottime changed from 1790735290 to 1790736421; config.xml-persisted interfaces (opt1/opt2/opt3) and FRR/OSPF service came back automatically at boot; Full OSPF adjacencies and routes recovered; bidirectional node3<->node4 ping confirmed
